svg.aria-label: One toy sampler step on 4 pixels: three calls, the two label differences d(3) and d(7), and their sum with the no-label guess.
svg.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: One toy step: three calls, two differences, one sum
Rose cells are what a label adds to the noise guess, d. Green would be a positive d; every d here is negative or zero.
1. Three calls on the same 4 pixels
label 3 acts on the left pixels
label 7 acts on the right pixels
No label adds nothing: u and v are zero,
so the no-label guess is x itself.
d(3) is non-zero only on the left,
d(7) only on the right. The noise x
cancels out of the u part of each d.
3. The product's noise guess, then one step
Toy step: subtract the guess. The real sampler
is DDIM, 50 steps, which scales each part.
A hand-set toy: 4 pixels, 2 steps, integer weights. It shows where each term sits and predicts nothing about the digit models. Numbers: miniature_answer_key.json, steps[0].
